ai.description: This slender snake reaches 60–80 cm. It is dark brown to black with a diagnostic bright yellow or orange nuchal collar and a white labial region. The body features a cylindrical shape and smooth scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Lycodon flavicollis* is the distinct, bright yellow or orange nuchal collar that contrasts sharply against its dark body.
ai.habitat: The Yellow-collared Wolf Snake inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, typically found in leaf litter or rocky areas at elevations between 300 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Yellow-collared Wolf Snake is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting for small lizards and frogs under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Lycodon flavicollis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–6 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing shortly thereafter.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Lycodon flavicollis* is found in Northeast India (Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram) and the Eastern Himalayas, typically inhabiting elevations from 200 to 1,500 meters.
